section.title: Goal
section.p: Build sxml (small XML implementation), an embeddable XML toolchain that brings XPath 4.0, XQuery 4.0, XSLT 4.0 and schema validation to every platform: browsers, Node.js, iOS, Android, macOS, Linux and Windows. The core is portable C following docs/C_GUIDELINES.md, compiled to native libraries and to WebAssembly from one codebase.
Success is measured, not judged: each phase ends when a named subset of the W3C QT4 test suite passes, and the public pass count is the project's progress bar.

The central design bet is a single XDM 4.0 value model shared by every language. XQuery and XSLT both lower into one intermediate representation, so there is one optimizer and one evaluator, not three engines.

section.title: Architecture
section.pre: C library API WebAssembly package Swift / Kotlin (Phase 6) \ | / XPath 4.0 XQuery 4.0 XSLT 4.0 \ | / Shared IR and optimizer | Evaluator -> F&O 4.0 function library Schema validation (Phase 5) | | Substrate (frozen after Phase 1): v XDM 4.0 values | XML tree (parser, arena) | Type registry | Memory interfaces
section.p: Schema validation arrives late but needs no substrate change: it registers its types in the type registry that atomic values already point into.

section.title: Scope for year one

item.p: XML 1.0 parsing with namespaces, into an arena-based tree.
The XDM 4.0 value model: sequences, nodes, atomic items, maps, arrays, records, function items, JSON values.
XPath 4.0 with the full F&O 4.0 function library.
XQuery 4.0 core language, including modules and higher-order functions.
C library builds for Linux, macOS and Windows; a WebAssembly build for browsers and Node.js.

section.p: Not in year one (each needs a decision record to be pulled in). These are delayed, not dropped: schema awareness is Phase 5 and the rest Phase 7 ().

item.p: Schema-aware processing and XSD 1.1 validation.
XSLT streaming and the XQuery Update Facility.
Collations beyond Unicode codepoint order.
A bytecode VM or any form of code generation.
Swift and Kotlin bindings, and Invisible XML.

section.title: Phases

row.cell: Phase
Delivers
Gate
0. Substrate design
Public headers for the XDM value model, tree and memory interfaces; glossary; golden files; CI with lints and sanitizers
Headers reviewed by a human; CI green on a compiling skeleton
1. Torture slice
Minimal XML parser and an XPath subset that exercises every part of the value model, in native and WebAssembly builds
100–200 hand-picked QT4 tests pass under sanitizers; substrate frozen
2. XPath 4.0
Full XPath 4.0 syntax and the F&O 4.0 function library; first public release
Agreed pass rate on QT4 XPath and function test sets
3. XQuery 4.0
FLWOR, constructors, prolog, modules, serialization
Agreed pass rate on QT4 XQuery test sets
4. XSLT 4.0
Templates, modes, packages, lowered into the shared IR
Agreed pass rate on XSLT 4.0 test sets
5. Schema validation
XSD 1.1 validation and schema-aware typing
XSD conformance subset; schema-aware QT4 tests
6. Platform bindings
Kotlin and Swift bindings over the host shim the JavaScript package shares (); Android builds for four ABIs and iOS builds
Binding tests on device in CI: Kotlin on the JVM, an Android emulator and an arm64 device; Swift on Linux, macOS, an iOS simulator and an iOS device (docs/tasks/phase-6.md)
7. Deferred features

What left out of Phases 2–4: full UCA, HTML parsing, invisible XML, streaming, the Update Facility, Full Text, EXPath, compatibility modes, timezone database, other calendars and languages, fn:transform (); proposed for the owner: xsl:evaluate, DTD processing, XML 1.1 input, disable-output-escaping. Large parts may be optional build features ()
Each feature's QT4, XSLT or xmlconf test sets pass at its packet's rate (docs/tasks/phase-7.md); earlier gates held; size budgets met

section.p: Phases 0 to 3 are year one. Pass-rate targets for Phases 2 and 3 are set at the end of Phase 1.

item.p: Headers are designed first and frozen.
Work comes in packets: one module or one specification chapter plus its test subset.
Golden files set the style.
Every change is gated by lints, sanitizers and tests.
A separate reviewer checks each change against the guidelines.
Substrate changes after the freeze need a decision record.
Conformance dashboard: pass counts per test set, published by CI on every merge.
Weekly log in docs/LOG.md: what passed, what's next, what is blocked.
Decision records in docs/DECISIONS.md.
Phase review at each gate.

row.cell: Risk
Mitigation
Endless redesign of the foundation
Time-boxed Phase 0; decision records; substrate frozen at the Phase 1 gate
Substrate proves wrong after the freeze
Torture slice targets the hardest parts of the value model first
Scope creep
Written non-goals; pulling one in requires a decision record
Agent-written code drifts
Headers first, golden files, lint gates, review pass
Memory-safety bugs on untrusted input
Sanitizers, fuzzing, checked size arithmetic
Decimal, date/time and regex take longer than planned
Each is its own packet, scheduled early in Phase 2
WebAssembly size
Size budget in CI; optional features as separate modules
Specifications still changing
Track QT4 drafts; draft-only features behind flags
